text_summary.body: On 7/V of Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year Nebuzaradan burned the Temple, palace and great houses; the army broke down the walls; the rest were deported and the poorest left; the bronze pillars, stands and sea were broken up and taken; the chief priest Seraiah and others were executed at Riblah.

setting.body: On the Babylonian (accession-year) count Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year began in Nisan 586; on a non-accession count, in Nisan 587. The fifth month is Ab (July/August).

assumptions: From 9/IV to 7/V (Kings) or 10/V (Jer 52:12): 27–31 days with 29/30-day months.

constraints.textual_assertion: which was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar
assumptions: Babylonian accession-year counting: year 19 = Nisan 586 – Nisan 585.

constraints.textual_assertion: which was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar
assumptions: Non-accession counting in 2 Kings (Young 2004): year 19 = Nisan 587 – Nisan 586.

competing_reconstructions.label: Day of the burning: 7th (2 Kgs 25:8), 10th (Jer 52:12) or 1st (Josephus) of Ab
competing_reconstructions.summary: The texts differ; no external source settles it.

competing_reconstructions.label: Year: Nebuchadnezzar's 19th (2 Kgs 25:8; Jer 52:12) or 18th (Jer 52:29; Josephus)
proponents: R. C. Young (2004): different counting conventions
competing_reconstructions.summary: Jer 52:28–30 numbers the deportations in Babylonian accession-year style (7th, 18th, 23rd years), one less than Kings.

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik dates the burning to the fifth month, seventh day of Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year and refers to Jer 52:17–23 for the inventory.
